pairs.question: Quid ergo, si quis chartas legaverit puras?
pairs.answer: Membranae non continebuntur neque ceterae ad scribendum materiae, sed nec coepti scribi libri.
pairs.derivation: Ulpian poses the question himself and answers it. Question is the verbatim interrogative 'quid ergo, si quis chartas legaverit puras?'; first word capitalized. Answer is the immediately following full sentence, which directly states what is not included when blank charta is bequeathed. Nothing trimmed; the preceding clauses (about chartae purae not being owed for libri legati, etc.) are setup discussion, not part of this Q&A.

pairs.question: Sed et pelles lanatae contineantur?
pairs.answer: Et hoc lanae cedere manifestum est.
pairs.derivation: Self-contained sentence in the run on 'lana legata'. Deliberative-subjunctive interrogative 'contineantur' = 'are woolly hides also included?'; answered directly by 'et hoc lanae cedere manifestum est' ('it is clear that this too falls to the wool-legacy'). Both clauses are verbatim and contiguous; only first-word capitalization normalized.

pairs.question: Proinde si quis servos habuit proprios, sed quorum operas locabat vel pistorias vel histrionicas vel alias similes, an servorum appellatione etiam hos legasse videatur?
pairs.answer: Quod et praesumi oportet, nisi contraria voluntas testatoris appareat.
pairs.derivation: Ulpian states the full hypothetical and the interrogative 'an ... videatur?' in one verbatim sentence (the whole scenario is needed for 'hos' to have a referent, so the question window includes it). The answer is the immediately following full sentence answering yes-with-qualification. First-word capitalization normalized; nothing cut.

pairs.question: Si filius ex uncia heres institutus sit et ab eo legata data sint, habeat et substitutum, deinde commisso edicto per alium filium accepit partis dimidiae bonorum possessionem: substitutus eius utrum ex uncia legata praestat an vero ex semisse?
pairs.answer: Et verius est ex semisse sed ex uncia omnibus ex reliquis liberis et parentibus.
pairs.derivation: Setup is widened to include the whole conditional scenario so 'substitutus eius', 'ex uncia' and 'ex semisse' have referents; all verbatim and contiguous up to the disjunctive interrogative 'utrum ... an vero ex semisse?'. The answer is the single following sentence resolving the disjunction ('ex semisse'); the 'sed ex uncia...' clause completes the same sentence (the apportionment) and is not a digression, so it is kept. First-word capitalization normalized.
